title: Smartvendor Store
subtitle: WhatsApp-First Commerce Brand Campaign
overview: A cohesive social media brand campaign for Smartvendor, a WhatsApp-native commerce platform that helps small businesses turn conversations into closed sales. The campaign positions WhatsApp as the only storefront a vendor needs: no website, no manual payment verification, just one chat, one sale.
problem: Small businesses, especially across Africa, sell most of their products through WhatsApp, yet most still run their store manually — juggling product photos, taking orders by chat and chasing payment screenshots. The result is slow, error-prone sales and lost revenue. The challenge was to make selling on WhatsApp feel fast, trusted and effortless in one memorable campaign.
solution: A conversion-focused campaign built around the hero message One Chat, One Sale. Each asset tackles a distinct friction: proving customers don't need a website, stopping the chore of verifying payment screenshots, and waking up to orders already sold overnight. A strict WhatsApp-green system, chat-first layouts and bold headlines keep the series cohesive while speaking to the everyday vendor.

features.title: One Chat, One Sale
features.description: The campaign's central message: converting everyday WhatsApp conversations into completed sales and turning messaging into the most direct revenue channel a vendor has.

features.title: Stop Verifying Screenshots
features.description: An asset addressing the biggest operational pain point for WhatsApp vendors: eliminating the slow, manual job of checking payment screenshots.

features.title: No Website Needed
features.description: Reframes the 'do I need a website?' question by positioning the chat itself as the storefront, removing a common barrier for non-technical sellers.

features.title: Wake Up to Sales
features.description: Sells the always-on nature of a chat-based store so vendors see their WhatsApp store as an asset that generates orders even while they sleep.

sections.title: Campaign Overview
sections.content:
Smartvendor is a WhatsApp-native commerce platform built for small businesses that already run their stores inside chat. The campaign compressed a complex value proposition — automated order-taking, catalog management and instant payment confirmation — into honest, single-idea visuals a vendor instantly relates to.

Every asset leads with a plain-language claim rather than a feature: One Chat, One Sale. Wake Up to Sales. Stop Verifying Screenshots. That turns the product into a feeling — a store that sells while you sleep — instead of a feature list.

sections.title: Visual Direction
sections.content:
The system leans into the platform's native environment: a WhatsApp-green palette grounds each asset in the chat context customers already trust, while clean whites and deep neutral text keep the series readable in a busy feed.

- Chat-first compositions: conversation bubbles, phone mockups and message UI act as the visual hook
- Bold headlines: short, statement-driven type carries one idea per post
- Consistent templates: a fixed grid, headline zone and phone placement keep the series cohesive
- High-contrast CTAs: green-on-dark and dark-on-light treatments guide the eye to the action

sections.title: Asset Breakdown
sections.content:
- 01. One Chat, One Sale (Hero): the anchor, pairing the headline with a chat thread becoming an order
- 02. Stop Verifying Screenshots: frames automation as time and money saved from chasing payment proofs
- 03. Do I Need a Website?: flips a common objection into an advantage
- 04/05. One Chat, One Sale (Variants): restates the hero claim in fresh layouts
- 06. Wake Up to Sales: sells the always-on storefront and a phone full of overnight orders
- 07. WhatsApp, The Better Way to Sell: the closer, contrasting WhatsApp commerce with clunky websites

sections.title: The Takeaway
sections.content: By anchoring every asset in the WhatsApp chat experience and leading with one plain-language claim per post, the campaign makes a technical platform feel like a simple, human upgrade to how vendors already sell.
